Gillian K. Hadfield & Jack Clark, Regulatory Markets: The Future of AI Governance (Jurimetrics 2026)

Hadfield and Clark identify two competing problems in AI regulation: a technical deficit, in that legislatures struggle to translate command-and-control requirements into technical ones, and a democratic deficit, in that leaning on industry for standards leaves values-based choices with private rather than accountable public actors. Their proposal is regulatory markets, in which governments require the targets of regulation to buy regulatory services from government-licensed private regulators, with governments setting outcome-based policy objectives and licensing against them. They work the model through red-teaming of frontier models and a hypothetical of seven regulators across three countries, and set out its limits, including the risk that competition fails for lack of scale. A twelve-minute detailed summary followed by a three-minute critical Oggy Assessment.
